subject.title: [Bug]: Agents should not be able to access or modify files outside their own working space.

question: Should OpenClaw enforce per-agent workspace confinement by default, and should that boundary cover file tools only or also exec/process via sandbox-required behavior?
rationale: Current behavior is an intentional compatibility posture documented as opt-in hardening, so changing it affects existing trusted local workflows and the security boundary rather than being a narrow code repair.

options.title: Define the boundary first
options.body: Choose the intended default, scope, migration, and docs before landing any code that changes agent filesystem isolation.

options.title: Land a partial file-tool fix
options.body: Accept a narrower filesystem-tool-only hardening path while explicitly leaving exec/process and absolute host writes as follow-up risk.

options.title: Keep opt-in only
options.body: Document the existing sandbox and `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` knobs as the supported answer and close the broader default-change direction separately.

recommendation.title: Define the boundary first
recommendation.body: Choose the intended default, scope, migration, and docs before landing any code that changes agent filesystem isolation.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant opt-in filesystem policy and current docs trace most directly to Peter Steinberger's commits, making him the best available routing owner for the security/default decision.
